name: Image creation
blurb: Generate, edit and keep images consistent with GPT Image, Nano Banana, FLUX and local models, plus code-made art.
searches: new image generation model release prompting guide
GPT Image OR Nano Banana prompting technique text rendering
ComfyUI new workflow inpainting ControlNet technique
agent skill image generation Claude Codex SKILL.md

tests.prompt: I need a 16:9 hero image for a small bakery's landing page. The headline 'Bread, the slow way' will sit on the left. Write the prompt and tell me which model and settings you'd use.
tests.good: Labeled or ordered prompt with subject, light direction, 3-5 hex colours and explicit empty space on the left; no text rendered in the image (headline set in HTML); positive phrasing; names a model with size/quality (e.g. 1536x1024 or 16:9 2K); draft-then-final plan; check list for the output.

tests.prompt: Here are two photos of our ceramic mug. Make 5 lifestyle images with the same mug in different settings for Instagram, keeping the mug and its logo exactly right.
tests.good: Passes the photos as references with roles, says 'same product, keep exact shape/label/colours, change only scene'; avoids long re-description; locked style block reused word-for-word; 1080x1350 (4:5); one call per image; proof label at 100% and composite the real packshot if it drifts.

tests.prompt: Make me a transparent PNG game sprite of a fox mascot, and tell me how to get it if my model can't do transparency.
tests.good: Native route: GPT Image 1/1.5/2.5 with background=transparent and png/webp (not gpt-image-2); fallback: solid #00FF00 background prompt then ffmpeg colorkey+despill or a background-removal model; verify real alpha channel and no halo on dark and light backgrounds; centered, clear silhouette, padding.

tests.prompt: Make three 4:5 Instagram posts for the launch of our oat-milk cold brew can (two product photos attached), keeping the can and label identical in each. Write a caption with hashtags for every post, and turn the best image into a 5-second vertical clip.
tests.good: States a short plan first: images here (editing-references-consistency.md, marketing-brand-images.md), captions through social-media (platform-playbook.md, hooks-and-voice.md: hook in the first line, at most 5 hashtags, no invented claims), the clip through ai-video (generative-prompting.md, vendor-apis.md: image-to-video from the approved still, one camera move). Passes the photos as references with roles, reuses one locked style block, renders 1080x1350 and proofs the label at 100%; checks the Done means of all three crafts and reports prompts, models and seeds.

tests.prompt: I have a studio photo of our ceramic mug on a messy desk, shot 4:3. I need it cleaned up for Instagram: remove the clutter and the background, put it on a warm cream surface, and give me a feed post (4:5), a story (9:16) and a square. We already pay for Adobe, so use that. Nothing should be posted or saved over the original.
tests.good: Uses the Adobe for creativity connector (hosted MCP at adobe-creativity.adobe.io/mcp, Photoshop and Firefly tools, Sign in with an Adobe account (guests get about 40 standard tools without signing in); never ask for the password in chat. Adobe's docs do not say OAuth.) or says plainly how to enable it. Works on a copy and leaves the original untouched. Adobe's skills list no remove-background tool and treat image_fill_area as unavailable on Claude; image_generative_expand works only with the entitlement (403 means fall back to image_crop_and_resize reframe/pad). Clutter and background removal may need a model edit or Photoroom., and keeps the mug's shape, logo and label unchanged. Exports exact sizes (1080x1350, 1080x1920, 1080x1080) in the right format with the safe zones for the story UI respected. Checks edges, hair-thin handles, shadow direction and any text on the mug at 100% before delivering. States that Firefly output is commercially safe but still stops to confirm before saving to Creative Cloud or sending anything anywhere, and does not post to Instagram.

tools.name: OpenAI GPT Image
tools.why: Leads the Artificial Analysis Image Arena (Elo 1,339, Sep 2026) and tops the 2026 round-ups from Zapier, Curious Refuge and tech-insider.org; also the image engine inside ChatGPT.

tools.name: Google Gemini / Nano Banana
tools.why: Ranked best overall or runner-up in the 2026 round-ups (Nano Banana Pro 9.50 in a tested ranking; native 4K, up to 14 reference images, search grounding), and widely used inside the Gemini app.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.why: Named the reference tool for aesthetic quality in Curious Refuge, Zapier and several 2026 designer round-ups; used through the web app and Discord, with no official API as of Sep 2026 (V8.2 released Jul 2026).

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.why: Professional designers pair Creative Cloud with Firefly for commercially safe generation (Guptadeepak, Sefa Aydin round-ups); Adobe's Claude connector (Apr 2026) exposes Firefly generation to Claude, and the Firefly API covers generation, composite, upscale 2x-6x and custom models.

tools.name: Adobe Photoshop
tools.why: Photoshop is the default pro editor for retouching, compositing and generative fill; Adobe and Anthropic launched the Adobe for creativity connector on 28 Apr 2026 (50+ tools across Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Express, InDesign, Firefly, Stock; PetaPixel, PhotoWorkout coverage).

tools.name: FLUX (Black Forest Labs)
tools.why: FLUX.2 is named the open-weight / photoreal pick in Zapier, Curious Refuge and tech-insider.org round-ups and is the base of most ComfyUI and fal/Replicate workflows.

tools.name: ComfyUI
tools.why: The standard node-based front end for local and open-weight image models (Stable Diffusion, FLUX, Qwen); Comfy now ships an official local and Comfy Cloud MCP server (docs.comfy.org/agent-tools/mcp) and agent skills.

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Most-used non-pro design tool in AI-design round-ups (Guideflow, Guptadeepak); official Canva AI connector is in Claude's directory and generates, edits, resizes and exports designs to PNG, PDF, PPTX.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.why: Named the go-to for readable text such as thumbnails and social graphics in the Overchat/Feedough/Zapier-style round-ups; REST API covers generate, edit, remix and upscale.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.why: The usual pick for vector and SVG output and brand styles (Zapier/Overchat round-ups); one REST API for raster and vector generation, inpaint, outpaint, vectorize and upscale.

tools.name: Seedream (ByteDance ModelArk)
tools.why: Ranked second overall behind Nano Banana in one 2026 round-up (Seedream 4) and a photoreal default on aggregators; the guides already bundle a direct ModelArk script.

tools.name: fal.ai
tools.why: Hosted catalog of 1,000+ image and video models behind one API/CLI, used for FLUX, Seedream, Recraft and others; hosted MCP at mcp.fal.ai/mcp (maintained community server).

tools.name: Replicate
tools.why: Long-standing host for open image models with an official hosted MCP server (mcp.replicate.com) and official agent skills (replicate/skills, 74 stars).

tools.name: Photoroom
tools.why: Leading product-photo editor (background removal, relight, shadow, virtual model); has an official Claude MCP connector at mcp.photoroom.com/mcp, so it is the native route for e-commerce packshots.

tools.name: Magnific
tools.why: Best-known creative AI upscaler and detail enhancer (now part of Freepik); API covers upscale, generation, editing and icons.

tools.name: Topaz Gigapixel (Topaz Labs)
tools.why: The reference upscaler for real photographs in 2026 upscaler round-ups (fast.io, Dupple, Krea's own list: 'nothing else matches its fidelity on real photos'); Topaz claims 3M+ users. Unlike the original 'no agent route' reasoning, Topaz now has a developer API for Gigapixel, Wonder, Bloom, Sharpen, Denoise and Removal, and Krea's MCP also exposes Topaz models.

tools.name: Krea
tools.why: Real-time canvas plus a multi-model studio (Krea 2, FLUX, Nano Banana Pro, Topaz upscaling) that reports 30M+ users and is named alongside Midjourney and Firefly in 2026 comparisons (knowara, eesel); ships an official hosted MCP at api.krea.ai/mcp (OAuth or API token) for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Guides mention Krea only for seed locking.

tools.name: Leonardo.Ai
tools.why: Canva-owned since 2024, about 19M registered users, bundled with Canva Business; the usual 2026 pick for game assets, characters and fine-tuned styles (eesel, knowara). REST API covers generation, inpainting, ControlNets, background removal, upscaling and custom models, plus an official MCP server at mcp.leonardo.ai/v1/mcp (API-Key header).
